status_as_of_cutoff: local process / regulatory pause as of 2026-08-11. Seattle official records confirm a citywide emergency moratorium for new or expanded data centers over 20 MVA was passed as CB 121214 / Ord 127447 on 2026-06-09 and signed on 2026-06-11, with companion Resolution 32204 adopted on 2026-06-09 and signed on 2026-06-12 for impact studies. Seattle City Light's large-data-center customer class and conditions of service were passed as CB 121231 / Ord 127473 on 2026-07-21 and signed on 2026-07-22. The underlying facilities remain utility-approach/proposal-stage: official city materials report four companies approached Seattle City Light for five large-scale data centers totaling 369 MW, but no project-specific land-use approval, building permit, construction start, energization, or operating status was verified.
evidence_grade: A- for Seattle Council/City Light policy actions and official 369 MW aggregate; B for developer identities, withdrawals, and remaining 249 MW active-proposal figure because those details are from local/media reporting rather than accessible official city records.

actions.government_body: Office of the Mayor of Seattle
actions.result_status: Mayor identified initial steps, including a one-year moratorium for new or expanded 10 MW+ large-load data centers and City Light large-load policy development.

CB 121214 passed; later Ord 127447. The ordinance adopted a moratorium on filing, accepting, processing, or approving applications for establishment, expansion, or change of use to data centers and defined covered data centers as over 20 MVA with uninterruptible power.
Resolution 32204 adopted, committing to study data-center impacts on electrical grid capacity and reliability, water, rates, land use, jobs/economy, and public health.

City Light described a proposed New Large Data Center Load Policy for new or expanded data-center electric service of 10 MVA or more, including a new rate class, cost-based rates, customer cost responsibility, service queue, and demand-response requirements.

CB 121231 passed; later Ord 127473. The ordinance established new retail rate schedules, a new customer class, and conditions of service for data centers whose electricity demand constitutes a new large load.
